answer: One concrete defense is staked attestation by randomly picked verifiers. Each epoch a beacon draws them from a wide lagoon of unrelated operators, and every identity posts a small copper bond slashed when its vote conflicts with the sampled quorum. An operator running a thousand clones still needs a thousand bonds, and because the beacon assigns staggered private windows, clones cannot copy one another's votes or vouch for each other in time. The attacker pays per identity but earns one divided reward, so the marginal fake agent loses money long before it can sway a decision.
